title: Spam Fun demo: a pretend extended-warranty robocaller vs. the screener
note: Real recorded test call (Oct 17, 2026) between the live Spam Fun screener and a pretend robocaller voice. No real people or numbers.

lines.speaker: Our bot
lines.text: Hey there, you've reached this line.
lines.display_text: Hey there, you've reached this line.

lines.speaker: Robocaller
lines.text: Hi there. We've been trying to reach you about your car's extended warranty. Your coverage is about to expire.
lines.display_text: Hi there. We've been trying to reach you about your car's extended warranty. Your coverage is about to expire.

lines.speaker: Our bot
lines.text: Ooh, I love surprises. Is this about my car getting old and sad, or is there some kind of exciting twist here?
lines.display_text: Ooh, I love surprises. Is this about my car getting old and sad, or is there some kind of exciting twist here?

lines.speaker: Robocaller
lines.text: Am I speaking with the owner of the vehicle?
lines.display_text: Am I speaking with the owner of the vehicle?

lines.speaker: Our bot
lines.text: Well, that's a mystery wrapped in an enigma, isn't it? But I'm genuinely curious. When you say the coverage is about to expire, does that mean my car's been secretly insured this whole time without me knowing, or is this more of a hypothetical expiration situation?

lines.speaker: Our bot
lines.text: Ah, here's a fun question for you though. Do you think cars dream about their make and model, or do they just dream about open highways and the occasional car wash? Because I feel like that's what really matters to them, you know?

lines.text: Look, this offer expires today. Can I please get your full name?

lines.speaker: Our bot
lines.text: I see in your future... free contests, specifically at WePrize.net. It's a free sweepstakes aggregator, all the free contests in one place, and honestly, you'd probably have better luck win—
